@@ -0,0 +1,32 @@
+//! #1749: the footprint a whole-model 3D Pocket (and its stamped twin,
+//! Multi-Axis Rough) clears - the silhouette grown past its open edges
+//! (`machining3d::open_sides`), the setup's other parts kept out.
+//!
+//! Provenance: the "tool centre on boundary" containment public CAM
+//! documentation describes; our own design, no vendor material consulted.
+
+use super::*;
+
+/// `region` as the ladder reads it: grown past the silhouette when it is
+/// the model's own source-built silhouette (`source_built`, an untilted
+/// whole-model source); otherwise the picked or controlled boundary,
+/// exactly as given. `neighbours` are the setup's other parts
+/// (`keep_law::neighbour_parts`): the growth never reaches into them.
+pub(super) fn open_footprint(
+    region: Region,
+    source_built: bool,
+    tilted: bool,
+    src: &SrcRef,
+    neighbours: &[Triangle],
+    r: f64,
+) -> Result<Region, GenError> {
+    if !source_built || tilted || !matches!(src, SrcRef::Entity(_)) {
+        return Ok(region);
+    }
+    let keep_out = if neighbours.is_empty() {
+        Region::empty()
+    } else {
+        slice::project(neighbours, FOOTPRINT_SAMPLES).map_err(from_slice)?
+    };
+    machining3d::open_sides(&region, r, &keep_out)
+}

@@ -0,0 +1,41 @@
+//! The open sides of a whole-model 3D pocket (#1749): where the model's
+//! silhouette edge has air beside it, the cutter may pass the edge.
+//!
+//! Provenance: the "tool centre on boundary" containment of a machining
+//! boundary, as public CAM documentation describes it, read with the
+//! level law of this module's parent; our own design, no vendor
+//! material consulted.
+//!
+//! The level law erodes each level's target by the tool radius, so a
+//! footprint that IS the silhouette keeps the cutter's edge inside it:
+//! a notch open to the part's outside keeps a band a radius wide along
+//! its open edge, the full stock height tall. Outside the silhouette no
+//! part material stands at any Z (that is what a silhouette is), so the
+//! footprint grows past it by just under a radius: the centre then rides
+//! up to the silhouette edge where it is open, and where a level's
+//! material stands flush with the silhouette the grown band is narrower
+//! than the erosion and cuts nothing. Other parts beside the model are
+//! taken out of the band, and the erosion keeps a full radius off them.
+
+use crate::geo2d::Region;
+use crate::machining2d::GenError;
+
+/// How far short of a full radius the footprint grows (mm): a band of
+/// exactly the radius would erode to a zero-width sliver along every
+/// flush wall, so the band stays this much narrower and erodes to
+/// nothing there. The centre then stops this far inside an open edge,
+/// and the cutter still passes the edge by the radius less this.
+pub const OPEN_SLACK: f64 = 0.01;
+
+/// The footprint of a whole-model 3D pocket whose centre may ride the
+/// silhouette: `silhouette` united with its offset by `r - OPEN_SLACK`
+/// less `keep_out` (the setup's other parts' silhouettes). A radius too
+/// small for the slack leaves the silhouette as it is.
+pub fn open_sides(silhouette: &Region, r: f64, keep_out: &Region) -> Result<Region, GenError> {
+    let grow = r - OPEN_SLACK;
+    if !grow.is_finite() || grow <= 0.0 || silhouette.is_empty() {
+        return Ok(silhouette.clone());
+    }
+    let band = silhouette.offset(grow)?.difference(keep_out)?;
+    Ok(silhouette.union(&band)?)
+}

@@ -0,0 +1,48 @@
+## #1749 - a whole-model 3D Pocket's centre rides the silhouette edge
+
+**What was decided.** The source-built footprint of a whole-model 3D
+Pocket (no picks, no Boundary settings, no tilt) grows past the model's
+silhouette by the tool radius less 0.01 mm (`machining3d::open_sides`),
+minus the silhouettes of the setup's other parts. The level law's erosion
+by the radius then puts the centre up to the silhouette edge where a
+level is open to the outside (the "tool centre on boundary" containment),
+so a notch open to the part's outside is cut past its open edge instead
+of keeping a band one radius wide at the full stock height. Where a
+level's material stands flush with the silhouette, the band is narrower
+than the erosion and cuts nothing, so a plain block gains no ring.
+
+**Why.** Outside the silhouette no part material stands at any Z, so the
+cutter may go there; the old footprint kept the cutter's edge inside it,
+which leaves the ridge the issue measured while the op reported ok.
+
+**Considered and dropped.**
+- The stock outline as the footprint (the 2D pocket's #12 reading): it
+  would clear all the stock around the part down to Bottom Z, a much
+  larger change to every whole-model 3D Pocket's output - a feature, not
+  this fix. Stock past the silhouette by more than about two radii is
+  still not cleared by a whole-model 3D Pocket.
+- A full-radius band: it erodes to a zero-width sliver along every flush
+  wall, numerically fragile; the 0.01 mm slack keeps it empty.
+- A warning only: the cut can be made safely, so it is made.
+
+**Also decided.**
+- Multi-Axis Rough takes the same footprint: it is the 3D Pocket's
+  ladder stamped with poses, and `operations::multiaxis_rough_peels_the_same_ladder_and_poses_its_walls`
+  pins that the two are one ladder.
+- The setup's other parts now reach both kinds' solid law
+  (`keep_law::neighbour_parts`, the #1621 neighbour law) as a second
+  net. It also names a cut through another part standing inside the
+  model's own silhouette, which the ladder (islands from its own model
+  only) never saw before and which used to read ok.
+- `shared_face_bodies::the_sample_as_imported_refuses_the_3d_pocket_by_name`
+  (#1706) pinned the old law (centre a radius inside the silhouette) on
+  a 6.53 mm strip: no 6 mm tool fit, so the op refused. Under the new
+  law the pocket clears the stock along the strip's sides and verifies
+  clean, so the test now pins that (`..._roughs_the_3d_pocket_beside_its_silhouette`).
+
+**Not changed.** A picked or Boundary-controlled region stays the user's
+boundary; a tilted (3+2) 3D Pocket keeps the old silhouette reading.
+
+**Cost to change later.** One call in each of generate's Pocket3D and
+Multi-Axis Rough arms (`operation::open_side`) and one motion function; the other parts' silhouettes come from the job's
+existing `neighbour_parts`.
